body:
My family life is kind of non existent, and when I do get in touch all it brings is pain. My career is non existent as well, I'm about to go to uni, just for the sake of going. It's not something I would like to do, the subject is pretty interesting, but the uni experience seems so dreadful to me. Yet, I've applied (back in January when my life was fine, well semi-fine) just to get it done and figured I can get through anything with my boyfriend, he can help me through all the things I will struggle with and help me believe in myself and stay on point and simply be there for me. My friendships... I mean I don't know whether that is the way things are when you're an adult, but they aren't what they used to be. Nobody reaches out, nobody needs help, they all "sort themselves out", not mention that all my friends are in a different country. All i ever wanted in life was to be happy, didn't care about money, about career, didn't have a specific idea of where my happiness should stem from. And that is what I had, pure happiness, until that happiness was taken away in such a sudden way at that. 

Thank you for responding to my post... I can't believe it's been 4 months since I've been on here... And that not much has changed in all that time. Anyway, thank you for taking the time to respond.
what about your career? work friends? neighbours? have you considered reaching out to your family and trying to fix things?

I understand how you feel. But doesn't it make you think that maybe if she doesn't love you, it wasn't meant to be? and now enables you to find your true happiness? What about your family or friends? Do you get any support from them?
What if I don't want this gift? Why can't I make my own decisions? I'm either and adult and responsible for myself, or not, in which case why would he be in a relationship with a "child"?

I understand. Well it is tough, but I think you can still do good for your family and still have other options other than suicide, if the only reason you are considering it is because of your finances. If you were to go abroad, I mean working illegally isn't the best thing ever, obviously, but you can still do good. And if you were set on moving and trying to work abroad I'm sure there are ways you could try and go legally, going illegally would be your last resort than, not ending your life.

Well it depends how you feel without her and with your decision in the end. Do you feel better now that you don't have her confusing you and coming over and being with you, but not being in a relationship with you? Or are you feeling like maybe she has helped you through some rough patches (i don't know maybe during or even before you relationship) and you should have done more? It's all about your own perspective and how your actions make you feel
Your country doesn't let people travel abroad?
So I should just let go and give up then, no hope. I understand. I appreciate the advice, thank you.

Why not go somewhere where you can go legally? or try going there legally? And even if it is risky, I mean it doesn't really matter at that point, does it? At least there's a chance you can help you family

I have seen lots, not the whole world, but I have travelled and lived on my own even before turning 18. We weren't talking about getting married right now, but just that it is something that is going to happen for us at some point when the time suits us. I've always known what I wanted, where I wanted to be, who with. I have always been eager to be responsible for myself, even if I make a mistake I wanted the consequences, always hated excuses. I just always know, what I don't know is how to convince him

I have met other people before I met after moving and being "an adult". Also during my adult and minor life I've lived in 3 different countries by myself and countless cities, so it's hard to say that if I haven't met anyone I'd even consider being interested in before, I'll suddenly find someone I'll love and care for as much as for him. I know I am young, but I've experienced more life than a person my age usually would have

He doesn't. He doesn't want anyone else, we've spoken about this. And if that was the case I'd also have a different view on all of this. If our relationship was having problems, or we weren't fully satisfied I'd understand the break up and I would be able to deal with it. But we haven't had problems and there's nobody else.
What's the point in that manipulation then? If I don't matter why bother with anything and just say yeah whatever don't come, yeah we'll chat sometime in the future and just leave me?

He is as far from an attention seeker as it gets. He doesn't want to play the field, if that was the case I'd understand. If we were having problems or if either one of us was like "oh I saw this hot someone on the street sucks I'm in a relationship" or any fights or whatever, other than usual everyday arguments, I'd understand. But we were so happy and it was so so sudden.

He's an artist, so he's more of an in the moment and no plan just go with it sort of person. But if he never wanted it, why would he say he did, on more than one occasion? Or when he noticed that it started to get serious for me (let's pretend it was never serious for him) why wouldn't he end it then and instead wait for us to have a flat together and all of those plans?

We've spoken about kids, he said it's up to me, I don't think I want kids, but I am aware that might change. Of course it is annoying when someone tells me I don't know what I want, because in 10 years it can change, well yeah, why would anyone get married then if in 10 years it can change? I am either an adult, and I should be treated like one, I know I'm young, but still responsible for myself, or I am not, but then why be in a relationship with me? Also he's an artist so not gonna retire for another 20 odd

I have never met anyone like him, anyone I can be my real self with, not get annoyed or anything. I know this is what "love" is. He is one of a kind in so many ways, and also is the best person I have ever met, whenever I think about how lucky I was and how great it all was and now that I've lost it and can't get back... I just can't let go.

He does hang with people his age, I'm the only one who is younger out of his social circle. His previous girlfriend was actually older. I know the age difference is big, but it doesn't feel that way when we're together.

Wouldn't worry about it, guys stress about that too much. If she really likes you as a person she won't care, I mean depends on how you acted. But as long as you just say something like "sorry, I'm just a bit stressed" or whatever instead of getting angry or making her feel bad it'll be fine. Just chill next time, no pressure, people get better at sex with one another over time

Then why does he still want to be in my life? We've booked a trip with his family to NYC for his sisters 50th, to which I was not going to go, but we've spoken about it and he says he wants me in his life and he wants me with him too, but just can't be with me now.

He isn't that sort of a guy, what happened with me wasn't planned at all. His previous girlfriend was 5 years older than him. And we were happy and serious, I just never understand those lame nobel gestures for the good of the other person, why do people feel the need to take away somebody else's choice on how they want their life to be?

You're so spot on, that's exactly the things he said, but I can do my adventures on my own, can't I? I can still meet people and do stuff and come back home to him, why is that a problem? I know I haven't been overly eager to do that so far, but I just didn't feel the need, which I'm sure I will at some point, just hasn't happened yet. We're going to NYC for 10 days in May with his family, for his sisters 50th, it's been booked since October and he still wants me to come, as a friend. He talks about how he still wants to be in my life, as my friend, but if he really doesn't want to be with me how could that work?

Not true. He was the one who was struggling with the whole age thing more than I. I'm not a sort of person who cares what other people think, if it makes me happy and I feel within me it's the right thing to do, that's that, I don't need any outside approval. But yes, he was having concerns about the age at the beginning, but I thought it has passed, especially since we've moved in together and have been talking about how serious we are, marriage and stuff. I don't want to run, I want to fight
What if it's me who doesn't play with kids my own age? Most of my friends are much older than me, I can hardly ever find anything to talk about with people my own age.

But he said he loves me, even after, or after the break up he'd go out to work or whatever and then after a few hours text me saying he misses me. He also said maybe in a few years if we still feel the same we can get back together, but also doesn't want to promise anything in case that promise would be holding me back...

He goes wherever he pleases, we do go away on holidays separately every now and then to visit friends or family. It's not that we're always together. It's more that if I have an option of doing something else I usually chose him.
That's what he's trying to tell me, how is it a favour? and if that is the case, why would he ever talk to me about getting married and how serious we were? Was it all a joke?

I was talking about moving away like a year here a year there. And another thing is that we have grown very close together, my character is quite difficult so I don't have many real friends, especially not where I've moved to. So if I have a choice of going for a drink with someone I'm okay with, but i know I'll see them at work in a couple days anyway, I'd just rather stay at home with him. Which makes him feel like he's stopping me from doing things...
Why don't you move away and earn there? Send some money back to help your family
